stages.name: Data quality & profile
stages.detail: Parsed timestamps, sorted rows and checked duplicates/missing values.

stages.name: Exploratory analysis
stages.detail: Computed descriptive statistics, returns, rolling statistics and chart series.

stages.name: Stationarity & transformations
stages.detail: ADF applied to level, first difference and simple returns where calculable.

stages.name: Temporal structure & lags
stages.detail: Calculated ACF/PACF of first differences; decomposition attempted only when a period is specified or inferred from a known frequency.

stages.name: Baseline forecast
stages.detail: Established a last-value baseline on a chronological holdout.

stages.name: Exponential smoothing candidates
stages.detail: Tried suitable non-seasonal smoothing candidates; failed fits are skipped rather than fabricated.

stages.name: ARIMA model comparison
stages.detail: Fitted a bounded set of candidate ARIMA models; AIC/BIC and holdout metrics are recorded when available.

stages.name: Forecast & model selection
stages.detail: Selected Holt trend by lowest chronological holdout RMSE among successfully evaluated candidates.

stages.name: Residual diagnostics
stages.detail: Ran Ljung–Box on fitted training residuals where available. A high p-value means failure to reject autocorrelation, not proof of all white-noise assumptions.

conclusion: Selected Holt trend because it had the lowest holdout RMSE (296.335) among 9 evaluated candidates.
The ADF test did not find sufficient evidence of stationarity in the level series at the 5% significance level; differencing/returns may be more appropriate for some models.
Ljung–Box detected residual autocorrelation at at least one tested lag; revisit model specification.
Forecast scores are from a chronological holdout; results are descriptive and do not imply trading profitability.
caveats: Model selection is a small candidate search, not exhaustive Auto-ARIMA.
Seasonal ARIMA is not automatically fitted; provide a defensible seasonal period and sufficient history before adding it.
Ljung–Box is a residual autocorrelation diagnostic, not proof of all white-noise properties.
Forecast accuracy is not equivalent to trading profitability.
